source: No maker manual. Read from the panels, the port map we hand-read, the community manual at https://github.com/patman023/nysthimanual and its changelog.

lines: Four tap delay modelled on the Buchla 277. Patching an output back into an input builds a feedback loop, which overloads as the input level rises
The delayed signal at the full time set by TIME
The delayed signal at half the time set by TIME
The delayed signal at a third of the time set by TIME
The delayed signal at a quarter of the time set by TIME
One of the four inputs into the delay line
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, setting the level of the input on that row
A CV setting the level of the input on that row
The delay time, from 5ms to 200ms, default 100ms
Shifts the delay range to 50ms to 2000ms in the x 10 position
A CV modulating the delay time
How far the TIME CV moves the delay time, -0.5 to +0.5
Programmer is a sixteen stage Serge style programmer. One stage is active at a time, and the four knob voltages of that stage appear at the four outputs.
Sixteen stages, numbered 1 to 16
One knob per stage in each row, setting the four voltages that stage holds.
Carries the voltage set by the A knob of the active stage.
Carries the voltage set by the B knob of the active stage.
Carries the voltage set by the C knob of the active stage.
Carries the voltage set by the D knob of the active stage.
An input taking a voltage that picks which stage is active.
An input; a trigger there moves to the next stage.
An input; a trigger there moves to the previous stage.
Sets how many pulses that stage fires, 1 to 8
